newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases down on firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases down on firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes reversed an earlier increase to end down 10 basis points at 17.30 percent on Thursday due to a stable peso, dealers said.
"The peso has been closely linked to secondary rates and it dampened upside pressure," a dealer said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.8110/7.8210 per dollar.
Overnight rates reached as high as 18.15 percent in early trade on a temporary liquidity squeeze, analysts said.

"There was some pressure this morning. Some dealers who were long on liquidity may have racked up rates to take advantage of players who needed to pay off term instruments that required settlement," a fixed-income analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 25 basis points at 19.10 percent. Banco de Mexico drained 1.258 billion pesos from the market
by assigning three direct Cetes sales and two repos.
Liquidity of just 1 million pesos was due to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank operations.
